summary: SMOTE oversampling does not meaningfully change the minority-class F1 score by 0.003772 (difference of 0.003772), which falls short of the 0.02 threshold. Cross-validation across 25 folds (5 repeats × 5 folds) confirms this finding with mean difference of 0.000956 (95% CI: [-0.000990, 0.002902]).
primary_metric_name: F1 score difference (SMOTE - Baseline) for minority class (>50K)
methodological_choices: 1. Missing value handling: filled with mode for categorical features (workclass, occupation, native-country). 2. Feature encoding: LabelEncoder for all categorical features. 3. Train-test split: 70-30 stratified split with random_state=42. 4. Classifier: default RandomForestClassifier() with random_state=42. 5. SMOTE: applied only to training data with default parameters (random_state=42). 6. Evaluation metric: F1 score for minority class (>50K, pos_label=1) using weighted average. 7. Validation: StratifiedKFold (5 splits) repeated 5 times with varying random seeds for robustness.
verification_method: Repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation, 5 repeats with different random seeds (RANDOM_STATE + repeat index). Total of 25 fold evaluations for both approaches.
verification_result: NO - Finding is STABLE. Cross-validation mean difference: 0.000956 (95% CI: [-0.000990, 0.002902])
